import MilneLib.Sheaf.SemilinearModuleMorphisms

/-!
# Isomorphisms of semilinear modules

Equivariant linear isomorphisms descend to the fixed algebra. Conversely,
an equivariant map is an isomorphism whenever its restriction to invariant
modules is an isomorphism. This is the transition-isomorphism input to
gluing the affine modules in Milne III.1.13.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u v w w'

namespace MilneLib.GaloisDescent.SemilinearAction

variable (K L : Type u) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
variable (R : Type v) [CommRing R] [Algebra K R] [Algebra L R]
  [IsScalarTower K L R] [MulSemiringAction (L ≃ₐ[K] L) R]
  [IsSemilinear K L R]
variable (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
  [DistribMulAction (L ≃ₐ[K] L) M] [SMulDistribClass (L ≃ₐ[K] L) R M]
variable (N : Type w') [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
  [DistribMulAction (L ≃ₐ[K] L) N] [SMulDistribClass (L ≃ₐ[K] L) R N]

/-- An equivariant module isomorphism restricts to an isomorphism of fixed
modules over the fixed algebra. -/
def invariantModuleEquiv (e : M ≃ₗ[R] N)
    (he : ∀ (g : L ≃ₐ[K] L) (m : M), e (g • m) = g • e m) :
    invariantModule K L R M ≃ₗ[FixedPoints.subalgebra K R (L ≃ₐ[K] L)]
      invariantModule K L R N where
  toLinearMap := invariantModuleMap K L R M N e.toLinearMap he
  invFun n := ⟨e.symm n, fun g => e.injective (by
    rw [he, e.apply_symm_apply, n.2 g])⟩
  left_inv m := Subtype.ext (e.symm_apply_apply m)
  right_inv n := Subtype.ext (e.apply_symm_apply n)

@[simp]
theorem invariantModuleEquiv_coe (e : M ≃ₗ[R] N)
    (he : ∀ (g : L ≃ₐ[K] L) (m : M), e (g • m) = g • e m)
    (m : invariantModule K L R M) :
    (invariantModuleEquiv K L R M N e he m : N) = e m := rfl

@[simp]
theorem invariantModuleEquiv_symm_coe (e : M ≃ₗ[R] N)
    (he : ∀ (g : L ≃ₐ[K] L) (m : M), e (g • m) = g • e m)
    (n : invariantModule K L R N) :
    ((invariantModuleEquiv K L R M N e he).symm n : M) = e.symm n := rfl

variable [Module K M] [Module L M] [IsScalarTower K L M]
  [IsScalarTower L R M] [IsScalarTower K R M]
  [Module K N] [Module L N] [IsScalarTower K L N]
  [IsScalarTower L R N] [IsScalarTower K R N]
  [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]

/-- Bijectivity of an equivariant map can be checked on its invariant modules.
The reverse implication uses the effective scalar-extension comparison. -/
theorem invariantModuleMap_bijective_iff (f : M →ₗ[R] N)
    (hf : ∀ (g : L ≃ₐ[K] L) (m : M), f (g • m) = g • f m) :
    Function.Bijective (invariantModuleMap K L R M N f hf) ↔
      Function.Bijective f := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    let e := LinearEquiv.ofBijective (invariantModuleMap K L R M N f hf) h
    let g := extendInvariantModuleMap K L R N M e.symm.toLinearMap
    have hgf : g.comp f = LinearMap.id := by
      apply linearMap_ext_of_invariantModule K L R M M
      intro m
      change g (f m) = m
      change g ((e m : invariantModule K L R N) : N) = (m : M)
      rw [show g ((e m : invariantModule K L R N) : N) =
        (e.symm (e m) : M) from extendInvariantModuleMap_invariant K L R N M _ _]
      simp
    have hfg : f.comp g = LinearMap.id := by
      apply linearMap_ext_of_invariantModule K L R N N
      intro n
      change f (g n) = n
      rw [show g n = (e.symm n : M) from
        extendInvariantModuleMap_invariant K L R N M _ n]
      change (e (e.symm n) : N) = n
      simp
    exact ⟨Function.LeftInverse.injective (fun m => by
        simpa [LinearMap.comp_apply] using LinearMap.congr_fun hgf m),
      Function.RightInverse.surjective (fun n => by
        simpa [LinearMap.comp_apply] using LinearMap.congr_fun hfg n)⟩
  · intro h
    exact (invariantModuleEquiv K L R M N (LinearEquiv.ofBijective f h) hf).bijective

end MilneLib.GaloisDescent.SemilinearAction
